analysis.investment_thesis: CapitalNumbers is a debt-free, high-ROCE (26.5%) small IT services shop at a modest 8.91x P/E, but it lacks a durable moat and growth has abruptly decelerated from ~28% CAGR to just 2% in FY25 with operating income actually contracting. At best a fair business at a fair price — not the kind of compounding machine worth concentrated capital.
key_strengths: ROCE 26.5% / ROE 20% with zero borrowings — clean capital structure.
FCF positive 5/5 years; FY25 FCF ~18 Cr on 26 Cr PAT.
Promoter holding 74.67% — strong skin in the game.
key_risks: Revenue growth collapsed from 28% CAGR to ~2% YoY (98→100 Cr); EBIT fell 34→30.
Commoditized offshore IT services — no switching-cost moat, directly exposed to GenAI disruption of billable hours.
Post-IPO cash bloat (equity 67→171 Cr) risks ROIC dilution if not deployed well.
red_flags: FY25 operating margin regression despite revenue still ticking up — pricing or utilization pressure.
'Other income' spiked to 6 Cr in FY25 (from IPO treasury) flattering reported PAT quality.
Investing CF -77 Cr in FY25 mostly parking IPO proceeds, not productive capex.
analysis.detailed_analysis: Inverting first: what kills this business? A ~100 Cr revenue offshore digital-consulting shop competes against both Tier-1 Indian IT and thousands of boutiques globally with no structural moat — switching costs are low and generative AI is directly cannibalizing the billable-hours model. The FY25 numbers already whisper this story: revenue growth crashed from a 28% CAGR to ~2% YoY, and operating income actually shrank 34→30 Cr. That is exactly the inflection a Munger watchlist treats as a yellow flag, not a buying opportunity.\n\nOn the positive side, the business earns genuine returns (ROCE 26.5%, ROE 20%), has no debt, converts profits to cash (FCF 18 Cr in FY25), and the promoter owns 74.67%. At 8.91x P/E and 203 Cr market cap the optical valuation is cheap — but arguably cheap for a reason. Post-IPO equity swelled to 171 Cr; until management redeploys that cash at incremental ROIC >15%, reported ROE drifts down. I'd want two quarters of reaccelerating organic revenue and stable operating margins before reconsidering; otherwise pass.
